Definition: Jedajah, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Jedaiah is the name of two Israelites, the priest of Jerusalem named among the priests who returned, and the head of a priestly house whose children numbered nine hundred and seventy-three in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah. The same house is counted twice, once in each return.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God counts His priests by the house, and the children of Jedaiah came home in their hundreds. My position is that the return from exile is a roll call, and Jedaiah's house answered.
